To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

contrast-enhanced spectral imaging mammography (CESIM) is a new imaging technique that is based on the use of iodinated contrast material and that can provide a higher sensitivity than conventional mammography.
the combination of CESM and MG does not improve the diagnostic performance of CESM alone and that the combination of these modalities leads to systematic size over estimation.
CESM alone has a similar sensitivity as CESM plus MG and a better size assessment, and is superior to MG alone.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the detection and size assessment of breast lesions and the radiation exposure of the patient, which is of great importance for the patient and for the radiologist, who is exposed to radiation during the procedure.
the detection of breast cancer and the estimation of tumor size.
the question of whether additional radiation exposure from combined MG and CESM examinations is justified.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
CESM alone has a high sensitivity and is better than MG in size measurement and that CESM + MG has a high sensitivity but is less accurate than CESM alone.
CESM is an excellent imaging tool for the detection of malignant lesions in the breast and is superior to MG in the assessment of tumor size.
CESM is a good alternative to MG in patients with dense breast tissue, and it is not necessary to perform MG in addition to CESM.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
CESM alone is as good as the combination of CESM and MG, with a lower radiation dose.
in patients with dense breast, CESM can be used alone to detect breast cancers with the same sensitivity as CESM plus MG and with a significantly lower radiation exposure, and MG is not needed.
CESM can replace mammography in the majority of cases.
The main takeaway from our work is that
CESM can provide a reliable and accurate alternative to MG, with the added benefit of lower radiation exposure.
the addition of CESM to MG is not necessary, as CESM alone has a sensitivity similar to that of CESM and MG combined, and a better size assessment.
in very dense breasts, CESM alone is as effective in detecting breast cancers as MG and CESM plus MG, with the additional benefit of reducing radiation exposure.
